question.problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $AB=BA={I}_{2}$

II. $AC=CA={I}_{2}$

III. $C\ne {A}^{-1}$

current_example.problem:
Using the method of direct verification, determine whether the matrix $B$ is the inverse of $A,$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14285500/assets/c7b1313482dd6f5a0e390c177d5cbeaf23e229164f517793f5047238789c10eb.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
We must check whether $AB = BA = I_2.$

Computing $AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $BA,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BA & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B = A^{-1}.$
